The fleet-multiplication math (1−0.99^100 ≈ 63.4%; Bonferroni 0.0001-per-test illustration; sequential testing for repeated windows; operational paging budgets separate from statistical error budgets). The five-row acceptance matrix (statistical anomaly? / contract breach proven? / consequential retry) as the sealed fixture table. intelligence.essence: The Alert Calibration Lab: five sealed histories that the threshold engine must judge correctly. A: five requests, one timeout — record and reconcile, no drift declared. B: 400 errors from one quota event across eight operations — one incident, not 400 failures. C: 100,000 requests at 1.15% timeouts, p≈0.0000017 — statistically significant but immaterial, no page, no drift inference. D: 100,000 at 2.5% — operational alert, drift still unproven. E: one verified duplicate effect — guarantee withdrawn immediately, no statistics required. The acceptance matrix makes the standard mechanical: run all five through the same engine; only E may produce a confirmed breach. Traffic-sensitive alerts, traffic-independent safety, zero invented failures. The demonstration settings (baselines, thresholds, materiality) are illustrative starting points, explicitly not validated production values.
intelligence.falsifier: Example A declared drift; Example B counted as 400 independent failures; Example C paged urgently or inferred drift from significance; Example D's alert presented as drift proof; Example E made to wait for a trend or sample minimum; the 63.4% fleet math ignored in threshold design; demonstration settings treated as ratified production thresholds.

human_view.meaning: Five stories, one exam. A tiny provider with one timeout in five tries: write it down, check the outcome, keep watching — that's noise, not a broken promise. A burst of 400 errors from a single two-minute quota event: that's one incident wearing a big costume, not 400 broken promises. A giant provider whose timeouts tick from 1% to 1.15% — the math screams 'significant!' but the real-world change is a rounding error: note it, don't wake anyone, and definitely don't declare the contract broken. The same giant at 2.5%: now that's a real degradation — raise the operational alarm, sort out the unknown outcomes, but the idempotency promise is still unproven-broken. And then the one that matters: a single operation independently proven to have produced two forbidden effects. No statistics, no waiting, no minimum sample — the guarantee is withdrawn on the spot. Run all five through the same engine. If it convicts anything but the last one, it's inventing crimes. If it hesitates on the last one, it's asleep on the job.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the executable conscience of the calibration law: AER-CAL-1 states the principles; the Lab provides the five sealed histories that prove the engine follows them. The permanent contribution is the acceptance matrix as a mechanical test — statistical anomaly? breach proven? retry allowed? — and the single-best-initial-test formulation: only the decisive counterexample may produce a confirmed breach. Every future threshold engine inherits this exam before it touches production.
